Action 1 — Cap A's Product Set ad set to ₹249/day and freeze it for 7 days. |DETAILS|
  • Domain: campaign.
  • Entity: ad set 120255473094910709 "Women | Exclude | Product Set | 29/10/26", in campaign 120255473094850709. Ad: 120255473094860709 "Bangle Product Set".
  • Change: edit the ad set daily budget from ₹500 to ₹249. Make it in the same session as Action 2. Then make no other edit for 7 days, because the budget reversed direction twice already, which resets learning.
  • Why:
    • Root cause 2.
    • Profit term moved: spend. Weekly spend falls from ₹3,500 to ₹1,743 (₹249 × 7).
    • Status. ACTIVE at ₹500/day since 2026-10-31 04:26 UTC. On 2026-11-02 it spent ₹434.38, which is 86.88% of ₹500 (434.38 ÷ 500) [11-02 · get_ad_level_data]. The budget is binding.
    • Ad-level S/GMV against BE0.
      • Product Set ad: 16.66% in 10-26 to 11-01 (1.14× BE0), and 23.46% in 10-27 to 11-02 (1.60× BE0). The 7-day figure is ₹1,500.24 spend, 4 orders, GMV ₹6,396 [get_ad_level_data].
      • Bangle 1 ad (in the paused AI_Video ad set): 32.07% (2.19× BE0), ₹1,410.16 spend, 3 orders [last 7 days · get_ad_level_data].
      • I size on the worse reading (23.46%). I use get_ad_level_data because the 3-day and 7-day S/GMV in get_adset_rebalancing came back misaligned (282.63 and 402.82).
    • Trend. A's Meta purchases per day were 4, 2, 1, 0 on 10-30 to 11-02, at daily spend of ₹661.12, ₹752.88, ₹766.74 and ₹780.40 [get_meta_daily_performance]. The trend is falling away from BE0, so it does not cross BE0 within the next ₹2,000.
    • Marginal CPP. A's own response to its budget changes cannot be read from 7 purchases in 4 days. I used 1.1× the implied average CPP: ₹412.57 = 1.1 × ₹375.06 (₹3,500 ÷ 9.33 orders).
  • Effect (the bridge row, as changes from the baseline):

| Reading | Profit ₹/wk | Orders/wk | S/GMV | |---|---|---|---| | Worse reading, 23.46% | −₹1,552.26 → −₹655.39 (+₹896.87) | 9.33 → 5.07 (−4.26, 45.64% of orders) | 23.46% → 21.49% (−1.97 points) | | Milder reading, 20.02% | −₹1,109.86 → −₹414.88 (+₹694.98) | 10.93 → 5.94 (−4.99) | 20.02% → 18.34% (−1.68 points) |

- RTO is unchanged at the 33% account unit. - Orders given up are below half, so no rebuild vehicle is required by P1.
  • Checkpoint: judge at ₹2,000 lifetime spend on the ad set. On the ad-level figure that is ₹499.76 away (₹2,000 − ₹1,500.24). On the ad-set rebalancing figure (₹1,099.21) it is ₹900.79 away. Judge lifetime S/GMV from get_ad_level_data. Break-even needs lifetime GMV ≥ ₹13,661.20 (₹2,000 ÷ 0.15). That is 5 more orders at ₹1,599 (₹7,265.20 ÷ ₹1,599 = 4.54, rounded up).
    • pass → (S/GMV ≤ 14.64%) hold ₹249/day to day 14 (2026-11-12). After that, +20% steps every 24–48h only while 3-day and 7-day S/GMV stay ≤ 14.64%.
    • fail → Action 3.
  • Seller check: no creative, image or catalogue asset is touched, so both standing brand instructions are respected.
, Action 2 — Exclude age 65+ on A's Product Set ad set, in the same session as Action 1. |DETAILS|
  • Domain: audience.
  • Entity: ad set 120255473094910709 "Women | Exclude | Product Set | 29/10/26", campaign 120255473094850709. It is configured at age 25–65, open audience, female.
  • Change: set the maximum age from 65 to 64. Meta reads 65 as "65 and older", so this removes that band. Keep the minimum age 25, the gender and the geo exclusions. Do not narrow to 25–54, because 55–64 bought.
  • Why:
    • Root cause 2.
    • Profit term moved: spend and CPP. The 65+ band took ₹332.22 of ₹2,185.29 of A's spend (15.20%) with 0 Meta purchases [8-week · get_campaign_age_data]. The bands that bought were 45–54 (3 purchases) and 55–64 (3 purchases).
    • Team ask. The 10-22 action "ages 25–54, exclude 65+" was marked "no effect on A", because A was built later at 25–65. This action applies that rule to A. A team ask is taken unless a hard rule blocks it. None does.
    • Departures, stated.
      • The exclusion bars (30 shipped orders in the slice, or a settled loss of ₹1,000/week) are not met. The slice wastes about ₹264.98 a week at the capped budget (₹1,743 × 15.20%).
      • The pass case gains ₹228.40 a week, under the ₹500/week size bar.
      • I take the edit anyway, for three reasons. The band has 0 purchases. The fail case costs ₹0.00 on the data, because the band bought nothing. The edit goes in the same session as the cap, so the ad set resets learning once, not twice, and it is 2 days from its gate.
    • Sizing. Spend stays at ₹1,743. The freed ₹264.98 is re-bought at the other ages at 1.1× their CPP. CPP of the other ages = (₹1,743 − ₹264.98) ÷ 5.07 = ₹291.34. Marginal CPP = 1.1 × ₹291.34 = ₹320.48. Pass: 264.98 ÷ 320.48 = 0.83 orders. Mid: half of that. Fail: 0.
    • Status. ACTIVE at ₹500/day, edited in the same session as Action 1. Last 3 days' spend is ₹2,300.02 for A [10-31 to 11-02 · get_campaign_daily_spend_and_metrics].
    • S/GMV. Ad-level 23.46% (1.60× BE0), as in Action 1.
  • Effect (the bridge row, mid case):
    • Profit: +₹114.20 a week (mid), +₹228.40 (pass), ₹0.00 (fail). Formula: 1.18 × 0.15 × GMV gained, with GMV gained = orders gained × ₹1,599.
    • Orders: +0.42 (mid), +0.83 (pass), 0 (fail).
    • S/GMV: −1.62 points (mid), from 21.49% to 19.87%.
    • Upper bound, not used: ₹312.68 a week, if the freed spend were simply not spent.
  • Checkpoint: read the 65+ band's spend share at the ₹2,000 gate, from get_campaign_age_data.
    • pass → it is near 0% and A's S/GMV is falling toward 14.64%. Keep the edit.
    • fail → (S/GMV still above 14.64%) Action 3 applies.
  • Seller check: no creative or catalogue asset is touched, so both standing instructions are respected.
, Action 3 — Pause A's last live ad set when the gate fails, on the day a replacement launches. |DETAILS|
  • Domain: campaign.
  • Entity: ad set 120255473094910709, then campaign 120255473094850709.
  • Change: on a fail at Action 1's gate, pause the ad set. Pause campaign A once the ad set is paused. The paused AI_Video ad set 120255473094920709 stays paused (already paused 2026-11-02, so not actioned again). Launch the replacement from Ops ask 1 the same day, at ₹500/day.
    • If no replacement product has been named by 2026-11-06, hold ₹249/day and re-read at the next ₹500 of spend. Then the account carries one capped vehicle at a loss (see Effect). This follows P5b: no day without a running sales campaign.
  • Why: Profit term moved: spend and orders. A loss-making vehicle past its gate with a falling trend is stopped, not shaved. This is the stronger move for an entity that has lost since launch. A pause also removes all of A's orders (5.07 per week, 100% of A's capped volume). The rebuild is the seller's new product from Ops ask 1. I cannot size it until a product is named.
  • Effect: this action applies only after a failed gate and a ready replacement, so the bridge shows it as a line below the table, not as a row.
    • On a fail: +₹655.39/wk against the capped state (−₹655.39 → ₹0.00). Orders go from 5.07 to 0.
    • One-time cost of reaching the gate: −₹221.65 (₹499.76 of spend at S/GMV 23.46%).
  • Checkpoint: gate = ₹2,000 lifetime, as in Action 1. A pass cancels this action.
  • Seller check: the replacement product's images must follow the black-background and brand-identity instructions (see Ops asks).

Action 1 — Pause the LAL catalogue campaign. |DETAILS|
  • Domain: campaign.
  • Entity: campaign 120255065157520400 (Rabami 24/10 | WO, 22+ | LAL Aud | On product set). Ad set 120255065157710400 (WO, 22+). Ad 120255065157840400 (PRODUCT SET, catalogue).
  • Change:
    1. In Ads Manager, read the ad's delivery status, the product set's contents and the ad account's payment status. No tool returns them (Ops ask 1).
    2. Then set the campaign to Paused. Its budget is ₹500/day (CBO). Do not edit the audience or the ad.
  • Why:
    • Cause: root causes 1 and 2. Profit terms moved: spend and CPP.
    • Status: ACTIVE, ₹500/day, created 2026-10-24. The last spend was ₹7.01 on 2026-10-30. The 3-day spend is ₹0.
    • I depart from "don't re-action what is at ₹0 for 3 days". The status still reads ACTIVE with a live budget, so it can resume at any time. A restart should be a decision.
    • In W44 it spent ₹1,796.77 for 1 order with GMV ₹499 [W44 · get_campaign_performance_metrics]. That is CPM ₹572.22, 3.42× the Copy campaign's ₹167.38.
    • It has one ad set and one ad. The ad's S/GMV is 360.07% [W44 · get_ad_level_data], so no earning ad needs protecting.
    • Lifetime it spent ₹2,724.38 for 2 Meta purchases, which is ₹1,362.19 per purchase. That is 11.17× the ₹121.96 break-even CPP at AOV ₹599. Lifetime S/GMV is 170.59% [diagnosis, get_campaign_product_data_top_percentile].
    • It is not improving. Crossing BE0 within the next ₹2,000 needs GMV of ₹2,000 ÷ 0.21 = ₹9,546.54, about 19 orders at ₹499. It made 2 orders in ₹2,724.38.
    • The table's "pause eligible: no" comes from age alone. The ₹2,000 gate was crossed on 2026-10-28 (₹2,418.53 cumulative).
  • Effect: ₹0 forward, because it has no spend now. It removes the risk of a restart at W44 pace. At W44 volume it would have saved ₹2,000.31 (retrospective only, see the Target bridge).
  • Checkpoint: read W45 spend on 2026-11-10.
    • Pass → campaign spend is ₹0. Keep paused.
    • Fail → if any spend shows on 120255065157520400 after the pause, check Ads Manager for a rule or a duplicate.
  • Seller check: no seller instructions are attached or on record. The pause needs no seller approval.
, Action 2 — Launch one capped test on two in-stock products. |DETAILS|
  • Domain: campaign.
  • Entity: new campaign, named by the Revenue team (for example "Rabami 03/11 | WO 23–65 | Open | Vch2slD6+GBWsyZwb test"). It is its own campaign, so it touches no existing one. Products:
    • Vch2slD6 (Gold Elegant Heart Crystal Chain Anti Tarnish Ring Bracelet For Women), AOV ₹699, stock 10.
    • GBWsyZwb (Gold Love Script Anti Tarnish Ring Bracelet For Women), AOV ₹669, stock 8.
  • Change:
    • Sales objective, CBO, ₹500/day, lowest cost without cap (the same setup as the account's other campaigns).
    • One ad set, open audience, female 23–65, placements facebook, instagram and threads, as in the other ad sets.
    • Geo: all India, excluding Assam, Jammu and Kashmir and Bihar (the team's 2026-11-01 ask) and the same 43 zips and 1 location cluster that the current ad sets exclude.
    • Two ads, one per product, using each product's existing image or video from its product page. I could not read which assets exist, so the team member names them in Ads Manager (see Assumptions).
    • Launch only after Ops ask 1 (funds and delivery check) is clear and the seller has confirmed stock of 10 and 8.
    • Fund it from the paused spend. ₹500/day is the paused LAL budget, so account budget does not rise.

  • Why:

    • Cause: no vehicle carries volume once the losing spend is gone (P5, never leave the account without a way to carry volume). Profit terms moved: CPP and spend.
    • Evidence is thin, and I name that rather than hide it. Candidate table, settled window 2026-09-21 to 2026-10-18:
      • Vch2slD6: 1 order, profit 25.41%. Directed S/GMV is ₹66 ÷ ₹699 = 9.44% (the diagnosis printed 7.98% on a different basis; I use the less favourable one).
      • GBWsyZwb: 2 directed orders, ₹330 directed spend, ₹1,338 GMV, S/GMV 24.66%, profit -23.28%.
      • 0 of 11 products are eligible. Neither product has the 3 orders the table wants or the 10 settled orders P5b names.
    • This test departs from P5b's evidence rule, which asks for an eligible product or at least 10 settled directed orders. I accept the departure because both products are the nearest the table has and the test is capped (P4: thin evidence calls for a small gated test).
    • Pass is defined as CPP at or below break-even. Break-even CPP is AOV × c ÷ 1.18, where c is the W44 contribution rate: (−2,876 + 2,828.81 × 1.18) ÷ 1,923 = 24.02%. At AOV ₹684 (the mean of ₹699 and ₹669) this is ₹139.26. At ₹699 it is ₹142.32. At ₹669 it is ₹136.21. The best CPP the account has recently reached, ₹241.84 (W43 Copy campaign, S/GMV 95.44%), is a loss and is therefore the fail reference.

    • Cases at the ₹2,000 spend cap (ex-GST), AOV ₹684:

      | Case | CPP ₹ | Orders | GMV ₹ | S/GMV | Profit ₹ | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | Pass | 139.26 | 14.36 | 9,823.21 | 20.36% | 0.00 | | Mid (average of pass and fail) | n/a | 9.25 | 6,325.76 | 31.62% | -840.25 | | Fail (2 × 241.84) | 483.68 | 4.13 | 2,828.32 | 70.71% | -1,680.50 |

    • The pass profit is zero by construction, because break-even is the pass line. Any CPP below ₹139.26 earns above zero.

    • Worst case: 0 orders at the cap costs ₹2,000 × 1.18 = ₹2,360.
    • The cap is 70.70% of W44 spend ex-GST (₹2,000 ÷ ₹2,828.81). The fail loss is 58.43% of W44's loss (₹1,680.50 ÷ ₹2,876).
    • Stock binds. The pass case needs 14.36 units, which is 79.79% of the 18 units in stock (10 + 8). If one product sold alone, spend at pass CPP stops at ₹1,392.62 for Vch2slD6 (10 × ₹139.26) or ₹1,089.66 for GBWsyZwb (8 × ₹136.21). Low stock means no raise (P6). This test does not raise any budget.
    • Timing: Diwali is 2026-11-08. At ₹500/day the ₹2,000 cap is reached in 4 days. Orders placed after about 2026-11-04 may deliver after Diwali (S2A is 4.59 days).
    • Effect: a test, not a certain gain. Per week: pass ₹0.00 (14.36 orders, S/GMV 20.36%), mid ₹-840.25 (9.25 orders, 31.62%), fail ₹-1,680.50 (4.13 orders, 70.71%). It buys volume and information, not profit. I keep it for that reason alone, and the bridge shows the mid case misses the target.
    • Checkpoint: ₹2,000 of lifetime spend on the new campaign. Under ₹2,000 no ad is paused for cost, because one order swings S/GMV by half (P5). The gate comes earlier only if both products reach stock 0.
    • Judged: CPP in ex-GST Meta spend per Shopdeck order, and S/GMV, against ₹139.26 and 20.95%.
    • Pass (CPP at or below ₹139.26) → keep running. Raise one +20% step every 24–48h only after the seller restocks and 14 days have passed. Ask for a settled-week read on 2026-11-24 or later.
    • Fail → pause at ₹2,000. Do not relaunch for 14 days. The next test is a seller-sourced product (the BS Bangles ask, Ops ask 4) or a lower-COGS listing.
    • If one product sells out first, pause its ad and let the other run to the gate.
    • Seller check: no seller instructions are attached or on record. The seller must confirm stock of 10 and 8, and that neither product has a pending cost-price edit by "system" (the diagnosis could not read the cost-price change log).

Action 1 — Correct the COD courier route to Delhivery express. |DETAILS|
  • Domain: logistics
  • Entity: account courier priority in the Shopdeck console, for COD orders.
  • Change:
    • Step 1. The logistics owner reads the live courier priority for COD orders.
    • Step 2. The logistics owner reads express serviceability for the pincodes of the last 7 days of COD orders.
    • Step 3. If express is not first for COD, set sr delhivery express first for the pincodes it serves.
    • Step 4. Take sr delhivery surface, sr shadowfax surface, sr xpressbees surface and sr ekart surface out of first priority for those pincodes.
    • If express is already first, make no change. The cause is then serviceability, and the owner asks Shopdeck logistics why express fell.
    • Target: express share of orders from 27.40% [W44 · get_logistics_partner_data] to 50% or more.
  • Why: RC1, S8, R26, R12.
    • Express carried 67.21% of orders in the PP and 27.40% in W44. It fell with no logged courier change [get_ts_shopdeck_changelogs]. The cause may be priority or pincode serviceability. Step 1 and Step 2 settle which.
    • COD only: sr delhivery express had 25.25% not-delivered on 99 AWBs, and sr delhivery surface 44.09% on 93 [W36 · get_logistics_partner_payment_mode_data]. In W41, express had 69.23% on 13 AWBs and surface 49.05% on 369 [W41 · get_logistics_partner_payment_mode_data]. The W41 express sample is small. The count includes in-transit orders.
    • All modes: express settled RTO 10.42% and surface 46.90% [W41 · get_logistics_partner_data]. Express held 2.93% of COD AWBs in W41, so this 10.42% mostly reflects prepaid orders. I use it for direction only.
    • W44 FAD, all modes: express 78.79% on 141 orders, surface 34.38% on 127, Shadowfax 35.71% on 79 [W44 · get_logistics_partner_data]. COD-only FAD is not held.
    • Funnel: the action does not move CPM, CTR or C2PR.
    • Expected ₹0.00/week in Plan size. The glossary has no formula for a courier move.
  • Checkpoint: day 3 and day 7. Read account FAD on orders placed after the change, against 60%. The guard is orders per day.
    • pass → FAD at 60% or more, with orders per day within 20% of the 7 days before. Keep the route.
    • fail → Restore the earlier priority for the pincodes where FAD fell. Ask Shopdeck logistics for a COD-only FAD by courier.
  • Seller check: no seller approval is needed for the priority. The daytime-attempt instruction goes to Delhivery in Ops asks.

Gender is kept because the comparable's efficiency rests on it, the entire catalogue is women's innerwear, and all five creative angles are written for a woman buyer; the explicit age band is dropped, which leaves Meta's default 18-65 - the same band the comparable ran - so no reach is lost and nothing else in the spec changes. DEVIATION 2, on execution grounds: the strategy's early read was per-ad CTR and CPM bound to the campaign, but a campaign has no id until it is built, so those reads are bound to the account. The kill-condition is unchanged and is read per-ad once the campaign exists: if all 5 ads sit under the 4.15% category CTR benchmark after 7 days and 5,000 impressions each, rebuild around the Rs.299 adhesive bra rather than adding spend. No roas_floor: the pixel has recorded zero purchases, so a floor would select LOWEST_COST_WITH_MIN_ROAS and the ad set would not spend. All 10 geo keys were re-resolved by me with search_meta_geo_locations and match the strategy table exactly: Assam 1725, Chandigarh 1726, Jammu and Kashmir 1732, Nagaland 1739, Pondicherry 1741, Punjab 1742, Rajasthan 1743, Arunachal Pradesh 1748, Mizoram 1749, Jharkhand 1756 - names sent in Meta's canonical spelling. Diwali is 2026-11-08, six days out, which is why the launch is now., Ask seller to complete 5 launch product pages, supply product videos, renegotiate cost and consider a 3-pack. |DETAILS| Instruction: Ask the seller to do four things before paid traffic arrives, and start today. 1) For each of these 5 products - 68V-rXYN (Purple Lycra Floral Lace Lingerie Set), pjxTGnT_ (Black Stick-On Invisible Adhesive Bra), S52WF_IQ (Blue Spandex Wire-Free T-Neck Sports Bra), msoPP3k4 (Red Lycra Full Coverage Seamless Bra), Td5ZUi-z (Black Lycra Underwire Full Coverage C-Cup Bra) - add a written description, at least 2 images and a size chart, and switch on the product testimonial widget with one testimonial under 45 days old attached. 2) Supply one product video per launch product, or confirm a UGC route for the same 5 products, since all 5 launch ads are video. 3) Renegotiate or re-source the catalogue toward 46.76% COGS - 66 of 68 products are currently 6 to 9 percentage points above that - and target a 10 to 20% cost improvement. 4) Consider a 3-pack offer on the seamless everyday bra, since the strongest comparables in this category sell 3-packs. The 5 launch products are named inside the missing-description and missing-size-chart sample SKU lists (pjxTGnT_, Td5ZUi-z, msoPP3k4, 68V-rXYN). get_seller_icp_score is 6.88 against a platform median of 8.7 and 90th percentile of 25.2, just under the 7 that the 2K-5K playbook treats as High ICP, which is consistent with those gaps: the catalogue is the constraint, not the ad account. On a cold account with no reviews and no historical buyers the product page IS the conversion evidence, and on innerwear the size chart IS the fit question - a paid click currently lands on a page with one photo, no description and no size chart. The sourcing ask is the largest single margin lever on this account and is deliberately a seller conversation rather than an operator action: 66 of 68 products sit 6-9pp above the 46.76% category COGS norm, worth roughly 8-12pp of margin across the catalogue, and the three price moves buy back only about 1.1pp of it on the launch set. A matched-product cost comparison does not exist for this catalogue (get_internal_pricing_similarity returns no internal matches), so the ask is to reach the category cost band rather than to match a named competitor. The 3-pack ask rests on comparables found via search_similar_products: uw3qoSBL 'Pack Of 3 Plus Size Bra' at 1,705 lifetime orders, 6yNmtCEi at 1,142, wlvN5HTd at 482, and Oqwp70ns 'Seamless T Shirt Bra, Cotton Full Coverage, 3 Pcs' at 372 - while this seller's catalogue has no multipack at all. Note the ordering constraint: the page work and the price moves should land together, because a price move against an unfinished page reads as a price rejection rather than a price problem., Update selling price for 68V-rXYN (Purple Lycra Floral Lace Lingerie Set) to Rs.649. |DETAILS| Instruction: Update selling price for 68V-rXYN (Purple Lycra Floral Lace Lingerie Set For Women) from Rs.639 to Rs.649 Reasoning: Current live price confirmed at Rs.639 by get_seller_catalogue and get_inventory_check - it matches the spec's stated current value, so no substitution was needed. No internal Shopdeck price anchor exists for this catalogue (get_internal_pricing_similarity returns no matches; get_marketplace_demand_validation matched only two inactive products), so this rests on marketplace pages read as search snippets - a band, not a point. The five price actions (Bet 2) must be applied before this campaign goes live - the ad headlines carry Rs.349/299/349/349/349 and a mismatch against the product page is a cancellation and RTO cause., Ask seller to open a cost-reduction conversation with the supplier. |DETAILS| Instruction: Ask the seller to open a cost-reduction conversation with their supplier covering the five launch products first, then the rest of the catalogue. Action 1 — Brown campaign: gated cost-cap test. |DETAILS|
  • Domain: campaign.
  • Entity: campaign 120248822475040464 "CPP | Premium Fashion | Brown Shirt | 19/10/26", ad set 120248822475020464, ad "Banner" 120248822475030464.
  • Change:
    1. First read the live cap in Ads Manager, to settle the units.
      • If it shows ₹120, raise it to ₹250.
      • If it shows ₹12,000, make no edit. The cap would not be binding, and a ₹250 entry would turn the raise into a cut.
    2. Change nothing else. Keep the budget at ₹500/day and the ad unchanged.
  • Why:
    • The cap is a hypothesis, not a proven cause. The campaign delivered ₹1,262.28 in 10-19..10-25 at the lower cap, and delivery fell after the 10-27 edits. A cap raise on 10-27 did not restore it, but it landed together with targeting and status edits, so the cap was never tested alone.
    • This test changes the cap alone.
    • It resets learning again. That is accepted because the campaign already spends about ₹13.31/day (₹93.17 ÷ 7), so there is little delivery to lose.
    • It is a CPP term test. ₹250 is below the ₹339 break-even CPP at the settled RTO of 54.41%.
  • Effect:
    • Pass: delivery returns to its 10-19..10-25 level of ₹1,262.28/week at CPP ₹149.09 (1.1 × its lifetime ad CPP of ₹135.54). Spend rises by ₹1,169.11/week and orders by 7.47, for about +₹1,361.98/week (k=1.0) or +₹1,151.54 (k=1.18).
    • Fail: the campaign spends ₹2,000 at CPP ₹500 and is paused. Spend rises by ₹1,906.83 and orders by 3, for about −₹889.83 (k=1.0) or −₹1,233.06 (k=1.18).
    • The earlier 13-order pass case at ₹3,500/week is dropped. It assumed the cap was the cause.
  • Checkpoint: ₹2,000 of spend after the edit.
    • Pass → CPP ≤ ₹250 and spend of at least about ₹180/day (₹1,262.28 ÷ 7): keep it. Take +20% steps only once it has a settled week of 10 or more orders.
    • Fail → CPP above ₹500, or spend still under ₹180/day after 48h: the cap is not the lever. Pause it and do not raise again. The next step is the fresh AI_Hits duplicate in Hold.
  • Seller check: Brown is a shirt, so it complies.

Expiry 2026-11-25 matches EXTRA10 so the two codes retire together., Set the partial-COD advance to 10% of cart. |DETAILS| Instruction: Set the partial-COD advance on the kidsbug checkout to 10% of the cart value, keeping the advance on cancellation and on RTO Reasoning: Item 11 of the work order named this operation alongside the two generic coupons; it is split onto its own action here because it is a separate storefront field and must be independently revertable. Direction and magnitude are carried from the strategy and checked against live state: get_seller_website_checkout_config confirms settings_payment_mode 'cod,online' with is_razorpay true, so partial COD is a supported mode on this checkout, and payment_charges_cod 0, delivery 0, min cart 0 - there is no fee stack to unwind. The refund flags matter as much as the amount: partial_cod_refund_on_cancel false and partial_cod_refund_on_rto false are set explicitly, because refunding the advance removes every reason the buyer had to accept the parcel, and the reason the advance exists is exactly the 73.53% settled RTO (get_campaign_rebalancing_rto, 9 delivered of 34 awb_nc) and the 17.4% NDR-to-delivered rate (get_seller_ndr_summary section B). The 10% rate is set as a percentage rather than a flat rupee amount because the cart range is wide - the strategy's flat Rs30 shape does not scale to a Rs499 toy and a Rs549 toy bought together., Enable the system bumper coupon at 10% up to Rs.100. |DETAILS| Instruction: Enable the system bumper coupon on the kidsbug checkout at 10% off with a max discount of Rs.100 Reasoning: Item 11 of the work order named this operation alongside the two generic coupons; it is split onto its own action because it is a separate storefront switch and must be independently revertable. The bumper is a post-purchase nudge, so it lifts repeat purchase without needing new traffic; it converts after the order is placed, which means it does not compete with the two generic coupons for the same checkout attention. Direction of caution, which is why the discount is held at 10% / Rs.100 rather than deeper: a bumper coupon lifts conversion and inflates customer-side cancellation at the same time on an account already cancelling at 2.94% customer-side (get_submetrics_data W44), so a deep bumper would work against the RTO bet. Rs.100 max discount on a book with AOV around Rs622 is a sane 16% ceiling at the top of the range., Add a Rs.29 COD charge (items 10 and 19). |DETAILS| Instruction: Set the COD fee on the kidsbug checkout to Rs.29, keeping the delivery charge at Rs.0 and the minimum-cart delivery charge at Rs.0 Reasoning: This action absorbs work-order items 10 and 19, which are the same COD-charge change listed twice, so they are merged here rather than issued as two competing payment-mode writes. Razorpay is integrated (is_razorpay true) and online is already enabled, so the prepaid path stays open and is the reason this can be a price move rather than a removal. Why the number is what it is: 97.59% of this account's orders are COD (get_payment_mode_level_data) and settled RTO is 73.53% (get_campaign_rebalancing_rto, 9 delivered of 34 awb_nc) against a 39.84% category benchmark - so the door problem is the account's dominant economic loss. A Rs.29 fee on a Rs499-699 toy is roughly 4-6%, small enough not to be a checkout barrier but large enough to make a buyer pause and either prepay or not order. The delivery charge and the minimum-cart delivery charge are stated explicitly at Rs.0 because both read 0 today and the seller has an unknown standing instruction on shipping pricing (no instructions attached to this run, none on record) - they are named so the operator confirms both rather than assuming. Seller consent is requested separately; if the seller declines, the fallback is to leave the COD charge at Rs.0 and keep the partial-COD advance as the RTO lever., Ask seller to remove the NEXT_DAY_DISPATCH trust badge. |DETAILS| Instruction: Ask the kidsbug seller to remove the NEXT_DAY_DISPATCH trust badge from the storefront and replace it with 'dispatch within 24 hours' - the badge promises next-day delivery while the checkout shows a maximum of 8 days, and 73.53% of parcels are refused at the door Reasoning: Item 14 of the work order. get_seller_website_checkout_config read today returns product_quality_trust_markers ['LOWEST_PRICE', 'NEXT_DAY_DISPATCH', 'SUPERIOR_QUALTIY_TRUSTBADGE'] alongside display_delivery_date_non_customised_max_day 8 and display_delivery_date_customised_max_day 8. A next-day-dispatch promise against an 8-day maximum delivery window is a promise the storefront cannot keep, and on an account where 73.53% of parcels are refused at the door (get_campaign_rebalancing_rto) the gap between what is promised and what arrives is the likeliest thing a buyer reacts to on the doorstep. The replacement wording 'dispatch within 24 hours' is what the strategy specified and it is supported by the account's own dispatch speed: get_submetrics_data shows o2s (order-to-ship) at 0.87 days, so a within-24-hours dispatch statement is true and a next-day delivery statement is not. The campaign is held until the renders land, so a decision before the renders finish is what makes this worth asking now., Ask seller to cut cost on MF-2005 from Rs.900 to Rs.849, selling price unchanged. |DETAILS| Instruction: Ask seller to reduce the cost price of Motiwala-Fashion-women-MF-2005 (Beige Mul Satin Straight Floral Print Kurta Set For Women) from Rs.900 to Rs.849 or below on its active SKUs, keeping the selling price at Rs.1,699 unchanged, and to keep this product unadvertised until then Reasoning: fetch_hygiene_actions (Hits bucket) returned 'Update all visible SKUs to have cogs less than 50%', and the flagged SKUs are the Rs.1,099 and Rs.1,199 kaftans and kurta sets — NOT the launch set, whose Rs.799 products are already at 37.5-45.1% COGS. Do not create price-change tasks for any of these three — they are parked products, not launch products., Turn off the checkout 'push for online payments' prompt. |DETAILS| Instruction: Set the storefront checkout setting 'push for online payments' to False on motiwalafashion.com, leaving payment modes as cod,online,partial-cod with cod first, and leaving COD fee, delivery fee and the online discount cap at their current values Reasoning: get_seller_website_checkout_config returns push_for_online_payments: True on a storefront whose settings_payment_mode is 'cod,online,partial-cod' with cod as the default, whose catalogue runs Rs.799-1,699 (impulse band, where a payment-screen prompt costs conversions), and which is spending Rs.0 today — so there is no prepaid-share effect to protect from turning it off. Note: estimate_audience_size returned no estimate for this seller (NOT CHECKED), so the reach of this spec is unverified - if the campaign under-delivers rather than converting, that is the reason to check first., Get seller approval for the 5 price rises and the 5 video creatives before launch. |DETAILS| Instruction: Ask seller to approve the price rise on 5 launch products - shopify_49328535666931 Rs 989 to Rs 1049, shopify_49313291403507 Rs 989 to Rs 1049, shopify_49313289601267 Rs 989 to Rs 1049, shopify_49313298448627 Rs 989 to Rs 1049, shopify_49313900527859 Rs 899 to Rs 949 - and to supply or approve one short vertical video per product (5 total), or approve single_banner per product where no video is available. The coupon and discount are raised, not set, because they change what the buyer pays. The catalogue's own-design nature is noted: get_internal_pricing_similarity returned no matches for any product and get_marketplace_demand_validation returned no rows, so every price in this plan rests on web-searched Myntra/Flipkart listings plus this seller's own costs, which is a weaker reference than a same-platform matched product., Raise Black Rhinestone Halter Crop Top from Rs 989 to Rs 1,049. |DETAILS| Instruction: Update selling price for shopify_49328535666931 (Black Stretch Mesh Rhinestone Halter Neck Crop Top) from Rs 989.00 to Rs 1049.00 Reasoning: COGS 50.05% (cost Rs 495 on Rs 989, get_seller_catalogue) against the womens-clothing category COGS band of 46.77% (get_seller_category_level_benchmarking) - 3.3pp out of band, and the hygiene sweep independently flags this SKU. Arithmetic re-derived: seller COGS = 345/799 = 43.18%, which is 0.42pp inside the mens-clothing category benchmark COGS of 43.60% (get_seller_category_level_benchmarking); that benchmark against this seller's Rs.345 cost implies a category price of Rs.791.28, so Rs.799 is +0.98% off the category-implied point, not above it. Because the Rs.345 cost is flat across all 34 products, every rupee of cut comes straight off gross margin and inflates COGS%: Rs.749 gives 46.06% COGS and Rs.404/unit, Rs.699 gives 49.36% and Rs.354, Rs.649 gives 53.16% and Rs.304, Rs.599 gives 57.60% and Rs.254 - all four outside the 43.60% band. A Rs.849 raise is defensible later (COGS 40.64%, gross Rs.504) but launching on an untested raise with zero orders of the seller's own risks the click; it is deferred to week 2., Ask seller to confirm the per-shirt cost price - Rs.345 or Rs.258.75. |DETAILS| Instruction: Ask the seller to confirm the per-shirt cost price on the live catalogue. At Rs.258.75 the same shirt yields Rs.540.25 gross per unit against Rs.454 today (+Rs.86.25, +19.0%) and COGS% falls to 32.38%, freeing Rs.86.25 per unit to fund either margin or a price move. No cost-price action is written on the catalogue because the retired-SKU cost is not a verified like-for-like reference for the fabrics being launched - it may be a different construction or a bulk price. Note for the record: 1ytKsA2t ('Classic White Paper Cotton Shirt For Men') appears active with 30 stock in get_inventory_check but has no catalogue entry at all (get_product_details_by_product_id names it as absent), which is worth the seller's eye as a merchandising gap., Add the missing Bestseller Infinite Product Widget to the storefront. |DETAILS| Instruction: Add the Bestseller Infinite Product Widget (id VRS4X8xGsC) to the store front pages on mishchipi.in, so a shopper on one shirt page can scroll straight into another shirt. On a catalogue of 34 near-identical shirts (9 whites and greys, 7 checks/plaid/stripes, 6 linen, all Rs.799) the widget is the only in-page route to a different colour or pattern, so it is directly relevant to this launch. widget_page_id and widget_page_type are left unset on purpose: no tool in this suite returns storefront page ids, and an unset field is never approximated - the widget id and the instruction text carry the change and a growth lead sets the page by hand. get_seller_catalogue_quality_summary corroborates the rest of the storefront as ready: 34 live products, 0 out of stock, 0 missing cost price, 0 with under 2 images, 0 missing size chart, 0 missing description, 0 untagged, 2/2 page templates present., Ask seller to approve a coupon ladder at Rs.1,598 and Rs.2,397 bands. |DETAILS| Instruction: Ask the seller to approve a two-band generic coupon ladder on mishchipi.in: one band at minimum order value Rs.1,598 and a second at Rs.2,397 (2x and 3x the Rs.799 shirt price), with a discount percentage on each band and an online-payment cap. Launch one Open Audience campaign on 5 repriced pet products at Rs 1,000/day. |DETAILS| Instruction: Create one campaign 'PetNMed - Launch - Open Audience - Pet Accessories' on Meta ad account 2129843837630433, Open Audience, Rs 1,000/day, one ad set holding 5 video ads on the 5 repriced products, age 18-65 all genders India excluding Assam and Bihar. Reasoning: Pre-live account: get_seller_account_age reports the seller has never recorded marketing spend, get_meta_campaign_settings found no campaigns at all, and get_seller_active_adsets returned none - so there is nothing to pause or restructure and this create is genuinely the account's first. Rs 1,000/day is the mandated first-campaign budget for a Hit account and takes total account spend from Rs 0 to Rs 1,000/day. No roas_floor is set deliberately: the pixel has never recorded a purchase, so a floor would place the ad set on LOWEST_COST_WITH_MIN_ROAS with no ratio for Meta to bid against and the campaign would read as dead rather than as a floor set too high. Leaving it unset runs LOWEST_COST_WITHOUT_CAP. Targeting is copied from what three independent comparable sellers used to convert (get_adset_details_for_product_id: adset 120231645397830715 at S/GMV 18.52%, adset 120236059732250658 at 19.17%, adset 6899188637577 at 23.43% - all age 18-65, all genders, India-wide excluding only Assam and Bihar). Assam=key 1725 and Bihar=key 1752 were resolved through search_meta_geo_locations, not remembered. Audience reach against this budget is NOT CHECKED (estimate_audience_size could not resolve an ad account for this seller), so the broad spec is chosen because comparably-situated sellers converted with it, not because it was measured to be fundable. Items 3 through 8 of the work order are carried here as notes because a Meta create builds campaign + ad set + creative + ad in one object - there is no separate ad-set or ad-creating action type, and the payload accepts ads inside ad_sets or ads at the top level but not both, so all five ads sit inside the one ad set. The ad set holds the whole Rs 1,000/day and carries the full budget because it is the only ad set; the five ads share it, roughly Rs 200/day each, so no single ad carries more than 20% of the budget. Optimization goal OFFSITE_CONVERSIONS, objective OUTCOME_SALES. Margin can fund it: cost is 25% of selling price, so gross margin is 75% before marketing and logistics, and at a Rs.1,199 cart the discount costs Rs.120. This coupon must go live before the campaign — the ad sends people to a page with an offer, and the campaign is held until its videos render anyway.
